subject: microbiology
title: Moist and Dry Heat Sterilisation: Autoclave, Hot Air Oven and Tyndallisation

steps.tx: The **autoclave** sterilises with saturated steam under pressure: 121 degrees Celsius at 15 pounds per square inch for 15 to 20 minutes kills vegetative bacteria, viruses and the benchmark spores by denaturing proteins with moisture's efficient heat transfer. Gravity and prevacuum cycles, load wrapping and air removal decide whether the centre of the pack ever meets steam, which is why cycle parameters are validated per load, not per machine dial.
steps.say: 121 degrees, 15 pounds, 15 minutes: steam under pressure is sterilisation's benchmark sentence.

left.title: Standard cycles
points: 121 C at 15 psi for 15 to 20 minutes (wrapped loads longer)
134 C for 3 to 4 minutes (prevacuum flash traditions)

right.title: Suitable loads
points: Culture media (sugar media excepted at lower settings)
Rubber and most plastics rated for steam
Never oils, powders or closed sealed containers

steps.tx: The **autoclave** sterilises with saturated steam under pressure. At 121 degrees Celsius and 15 pounds per square inch, held for 15 to 20 minutes, moisture denatures proteins and kills vegetative bacteria, viruses, and the spores used as the benchmark. Gravity displacement and prevacuum cycles are not interchangeable. Wrapping, packing density, and removal of air decide whether steam ever reaches the centre of a pack. A dial reading on the machine does not prove the load was sterilised. Parameters have to be validated for each kind of load.
steps.say: Saturated steam at 121 degrees Celsius and 15 pounds per square inch for 15 to 20 minutes is the autoclave benchmark. Moisture kills vegetative organisms, viruses, and spores by denaturing protein. Gravity or prevacuum cycles, wrapping, and air removal decide if the pack centre is actually steamed. Validation belongs to the load, not only the dial.

vis.alt: A diagram shows an autoclave chamber loaded with wrapped packs and the saturated steam cycle of temperature, pressure, and time.
vis.caption: Wrapped packs sit in a pressure chamber while saturated steam at 121 degrees Celsius and 15 pounds per square inch is driven through the load. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Moist heat kills at lower temperatures than dry heat because water denatures and coagulates protein efficiently and steam condensing on cool loads releases latent heat exactly where needed; dry heat must oxidise, demanding the **hot air oven**'s 160 degrees for two hours (or 170 for one, 180 for thirty minutes). Oils, powders, glassware and sharp instruments that steam would dull or corrode take the dry route.
steps.say: Steam denatures wet and fast; dry heat oxidises slow and hot. Match load to physics.

steps.tx: **Tyndallisation** (fractional sterilisation) outwits spores by patience: steam at 100 degrees for thirty minutes on three successive days kills vegetative cells day one, lets surviving spores germinate overnight in the nutrient medium, and kills the hatchlings on days two and three. It served heat sensitive sugar and egg media before filtration and autoclave safe formulations retired it to examination permanence.
steps.say: Three days of steaming ambush spores at germination; patience substitutes for pressure.

nodes.label: Day 1 steam: vegetative cells die, spores survive

steps.tx: **Sterilisation monitoring is** three layered: physical (cycle printouts of time, temperature, pressure), chemical (autoclave tape and integrators changing colour, Bowie Dick tests for air removal in prevacuum sterilisers), and biological (Geobacillus stearothermophilus spore ampoules incubated after the cycle, growth meaning failure). Biological indicators are the only proof that spores died, the same organism this module keeps appointing as referee.
steps.say: Tape proves exposure, printouts prove parameters, spores prove sterilisation.

left.title: Indicator layers
points: Chemical: tape, strips, Bowie Dick daily
Biological: G stearothermophilus spores weekly and per implant load
Failed biological: recall loads since last pass

right.title: Dry heat referee
points: Chemical indicators for hot air cycles

steps.tx: **Sterilisation monitoring** has three layers. Physical records print time, temperature, and pressure for the cycle. Chemical indicators include autoclave tape and integrators that change colour, plus the Bowie Dick test for air removal in prevacuum sterilisers. Biological indicators are ampoules of Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores incubated after the cycle. Growth means the cycle failed. Only those spores prove that the most resistant benchmark organisms actually died. Tape and printouts show exposure and machine settings. They do not, by themselves, prove sterilisation.
steps.say: Monitoring stacks physical printouts, chemical colour change, and live spores. Tape and integrators show exposure. The Bowie Dick test checks air removal in prevacuum machines. Geobacillus stearothermophilus ampoules are incubated after the cycle, and growth means failure. Only that biological result proves spores died.

vis.alt: A pair of biological indicator ampoules shows no growth before incubation and a colour change or turbidity after a failed sterilisation cycle.
vis.caption: Spore ampoules look unchanged immediately after the cycle, then one turns turbid or changes colour if Geobacillus stearothermophilus grows on incubation. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Below sterilisation sit** the heat disinfections: boiling at 100 degrees for 10 to 30 minutes kills vegetative pathogens (hepatitis B virus included with time) but not spores, pasteurisation trims milk pathogens at defined curves, and inspissation solidifies egg media (Lowenstein Jensen) at 80 to 85 degrees over days while disinfecting gently. Naming the level correctly (sterilisation versus disinfection) is itself an examination answer.
steps.say: Boiling disinfects, autoclaving sterilises; the difference is spores, and examiners charge for it.

left.title: Heat disinfection
points: Boiling 100 C: vegetative kill, spores survive
Inspissation: egg media set at 80 to 85 C
Hot water disinfection for linen and utensils

right.title: Full sterilisation
points: Autoclave and hot air oven cycles

steps.tx: **Autoclave failure modes** are load crimes, not machine mysteries: overpacking, sealed containers, air trapped in lumens and textiles, wet packs that wick contamination after the cycle, and cycles chosen for the dial rather than the load. Wrapped sterile items carry event related sterility (compromised when wet, torn or dropped) more than calendar expiry in modern practice.
steps.say: Wet, torn or dropped means unsterile regardless of date; sterility is an event, not a birthday.

right.title: Storage discipline
points: Traceability of loads to patients for implants

steps.tx: **Prion reality bends** sterilisation rules at the extreme: conventional cycles do not reliably inactivate prions, so instruments from high risk tissues in suspected Creutzfeldt Jakob disease take extended prevacuum cycles (134 degrees for 18 minutes), sodium hydroxide soaks, or single use destruction pathways. The spore benchmark fails here, and policy, not habit, decides instrument fate.
steps.say: Prions outlast spore cycles; suspected CJD instruments follow destruction pathways, not routine ones.

left.title: Prion facts
points: High risk tissues: brain, dura, posterior eye
Extended cycles plus NaOH in protocols

right.title: Policy responses
points: Single use instruments for high risk cases

steps.tx: **Choosing a sterilisation** method is a four question algorithm asked per item: does it tolerate moisture, does it tolerate heat, is it a fluid or device, and what bioburden and material (oils, powders, lumens, electronics) constrain contact. This algorithm, not memorised lists, answers the viva variations examiners improvise around autoclave and oven.
steps.say: Moisture, heat, fluid or device, material: four questions choose every sterilisation method.

nodes.label: Heat yes, moisture no (oils, powders)? Hot air oven
Heat labile device? EtO, plasma or chemical
